messages:
sam_support: FYI AcmeCorp is hitting repeated 502/504s on hosted /v1/generate during their morning batch window starting ~01:20 UTC. They see bursts every ~30s that last 10–20s. SDK shows retry storms. They're on region: us-west-2. Logs attached by customer (see below).

ingrid_support: Thanks Sam — can you paste the first few error lines? Also any customer request headers (client-id, sdk version)?

sam_support: Paste from customer: `errors: [502, 504, 502, 502, 504]` repeated. They included this curl snippet: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'X-Client-ID: acme-batcher-12' -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"...","batch_size":16}'`

tariq_sre: Oncall — can we correlate with edge/ingress logs? Sounds like connection resets or upstream timeouts. I'll start a quick probe of the USW2 edge pools and LB metrics.

sre-bot: Incident probe started: query=edge.ingress.usw2.* metric=5xx_rate, latency. Time range=01:00-02:00 UTC. Returning aggregated spikes on edge-ingress-3 and ingress-7 between 01:18-01:26 UTC.

maya_engineer: Repro attempt: I ran a local multi-conn test against hosted with batch_size=16 and concurrency=50 from us-west. I see a few 502s from the edge, with connection resets after ~10s. Kernel p95 on serving nodes is normal. No model OOMs.

tariq_sre: Noticed SYN backlog and increased connection churn on ingress-7. Also short-lived CPU steal on the workers hosting TLS termination. Looks like the ingress pool got overwhelmed by connection open/close rate rather than steady throughput.

ingrid_support: Customer says they recently rolled out a new client that opens fresh connections per batch and disables keepalive. They didn't realize.

sam_support: Customer confirmed — their new batcher is short-lived processes and we see many short TCP sessions.

maya_engineer: Root hypothesis: edge ingress hit connection-accept throttling and started returning proxy 502/504 when upstream pools couldn't accept handoffs quickly. Mitigation options: encourage keepalive + connection reuse, or route them to a dedicated burst-capable pool (if on Dedicated).

oncall-kat: Short-term mitigation: enable per-tenant soft rate-limits to smooth bursts and add ingress-level backpressure (we can push a temporary 10r/s token bucket for acme-batcher-12). I'll put a hold for 30m and monitor.

tariq_sre: Also increasing max_sockets and accept queue size on ingress-7 as an emergency config push (non-disruptive). Rolling now across zone. Watch for improvements in the next 5m.

sre-bot: Config roll started: ingress-7 max_accept_queue=2048 -> applied to 50% -> 100%.

sam_support: Update to customer: "We're seeing connection churn on our edge causing transient 5xxs. We've applied temporary smoothing and configuration tweaks; please re-enable connection keepalive and retry with a single long-lived process — that should eliminate the retry storm. We'll monitor for the next 30m."

ingrid_support: Customer responded: "We'll reconfigure—can you confirm any SDK flags?"

maya_engineer: Recommend SDK usage: persistent HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 keepalive, connection pool size 8, backoff jitter, and avoid spawning new processes per batch. Example snippet: 
```
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 8, retry: { attempts: 4, base: 200 } });
```

sam_support: Customer applied changes and ran a 15m smoke test. They report no new 5xxs. Logs show steady connections and lower accept queue.

tariq_sre: Post-mortem notes: primary cause = client-side connection churn exposing edge accept queue limits during a small traffic surge. Secondary factor = TLS worker CPU steal on ingress-7 (investigate host level scheduler/overcommit). Action items: (1) add docs/guidance for client batchers re: connection reuse, (2) capacity tweak in us-west ingress fleet to increase headroom, (3) automated tenant-smoothing rule for sudden connection spikes.

ingrid_support: I'll draft comms to AcmeCorp summarizing root cause + recommended client flags + follow-ups.

sam_support: Closing thread after 2h of clean telemetry. Will upload trimmed logs and the customer-facing status message.

ingrid_support: Customer message sent: "Thanks — changes worked. Appreciate the quick response. We'll adopt keepalive and update us if you roll further infra changes." :thumbsup:
